title: Resident exam
description: Triage, ABCDE, order indications, blood draw and tube order, basic lab values, wound care, fractures, hospital drug doses, documentation.

questions.q: Which triage level does a patient arriving in cardiac arrest get?
What is the right order of the ABCDE survey?
What may be done in the hospital before triage (rule K10)?
answers: Any medicine may be given when ordered
Only the treating doctor may be chosen
Only the patient's details are recorded

questions.q: When is a head CT indicated after a head injury?
answers: Loss of consciousness, GCS < 15 or anticoagulant
Always, whatever the way the injury happened
Only when the patient complains of a headache
Only when a bleeding scalp wound is also seen

questions.q: What is needed before a cast is put on?
answers: An X-ray of the injured limb
A full lab with all the tubes
A head CT to rule out injury

questions.q: What is the right order of the blood tubes?
What happens when the EDTA tube is drawn before the serum tube?
answers: False high potassium and false low calcium
False high haemoglobin and false low sodium
False low glucose and false high troponin
Long INR and a false low white cell count

questions.q: What is the typical error of a haemolysed sample?
What does an underfilled citrate tube cause?
What is the normal haemoglobin range of an adult man?
What is the normal serum potassium range?
What do a high lactate and a low pH together point to?
What does a high troponin point to?
What is the first step of treating a dirty cut in the wound room?
When is tetanus prophylaxis needed in wound care?
answers: When the last shot was over 10 years ago or unknown
Only when the wound is visibly infected with pus
Only for injured patients over the age of sixty
Never, when the wound has been washed out well

questions.q: What happens when you suture without local anaesthesia?
answers: The patient moves, the suture gets worse
The wound heals faster, with less scarring
The patient's blood pressure drops sharply
The suture fails automatically every time

questions.q: In a displaced forearm fracture, what is the order in the cast room?
What must be checked after the cast is on?
answers: Glucose, lactate and the pH value
Pupils, the GCS and the speech

questions.q: What does a cast that is too tight show?
answers: Rising pain, pale and cold fingers
Mild itching under the cast's edge
Slightly warm skin around the cast
The surface of the cast dries fast

questions.q: Why is pain relief needed before a reduction?
answers: In pain the patient resists and the reduction is worse
Because the painkiller speeds up the bone's healing
Because without it the X-ray cannot be read later
Because the cast only sets with a painkiller given

questions.q: How many diagnoses (ICD) can a case have?
answers: At most 5, there is no main one
At most 10, the first is the main
Any number, all of equal rank

questions.q: What happens when you order a test without an indication?
answers: Only half of the points are given
The test is never carried out
The order is cancelled at once
Double points are given for it

questions.q: When may a star (*) ICD code be given?
answers: Only next to a dagger (+) code
Any time, as a diagnosis alone

questions.q: In whose language is the Ambulatory sheet stored?
answers: The author's; coded parts show in the reader's language
Always Hungarian, translated when it is opened
Always English, as the hospital is international
The patient's, which must be set at admission

questions.q: What happens to the Ambulatory sheet when a patient is taken back?
answers: A new version is made at closing
The old sheet is deleted for good
The sheet can never be changed
The patient gets a new case number

questions.q: How long is a ward stay when the patient is stable?
What happens when a ward patient deteriorates?
answers: The timer stops and the treating doctor is alerted
The patient moves to the ICU automatically
The patient goes home, the case closes with an error
Nothing, the timer keeps running to the end

questions.q: Within what time must an S2 transfer happen (in game time)?
Who may request an S2 transfer?
Which need makes the transfer an ALS-only job?
answers: Oxygen, a syringe pump, ventilation or a monitor
When the patient is male and over sixty years
When the target hospital is more than 2 km away
When the patient asked to be transferred

questions.q: Where in the hospital may RSI and intubation be done (conscious patient)?
answers: In the shock room or the ICU
Anywhere in the corridor on a trolley
Only behind the X-ray control desk

questions.q: Where must you stand when the X-ray is taken?
answers: At the control desk behind the lead wall
Next to the patient, at the foot end
Outside in the corridor by the door
In front of the wall viewer, centred

questions.q: What happens with a limb X-ray when the wrong side is ordered?
answers: A negative image is made and the test is not indicated
The system corrects it to the right side by itself
Both sides are imaged with no extra cost at all
The image is made but never goes into the pathway

questions.q: What is the FAST exam for?
answers: Looking for free fluid and pneumothorax
Showing the exact course of a fracture

questions.q: What do you do when a FAST window is not evaluable?
answers: Repeat the exam or order a CT
Send the patient home at once

questions.q: Where in the hospital can a 12-lead ECG be taken?
answers: In the shock room, where the ECG machine is
At any ward bed from the bedside monitor
In the corridor without any monitor
In the X-ray room during the exposure

questions.q: What does a negative lead I with a positive aVR show?
answers: Swapped right and left arm electrodes
Severe hypokalaemia and a long QT

questions.q: What is the usual adult dose of metamizole?
What is the usual first dose of morphine for an adult?
What is the usual dose of ondansetron?
What is the dose of tranexamic acid in a bleeding trauma patient?
What does a nurse need before giving a medicine?
answers: A drug order on the patient panel
An EMS bag from the ambulance station

questions.q: How does the triage helper work?
answers: It suggests from the measured values, you decide
It sets the level for the patient by itself
It reads the level from the EMS handover text
At random, it was only made for practice

questions.q: What do you do with an unregistered patient brought into the ER zone?
answers: Push the patient to the morgue at once
Wait until an ambulance also arrives
Nothing, the system takes them in later

questions.q: What happens when you push an empty hospital trolley into the trolley marker and press E?
answers: You get a second trolley next to it
The trolley jumps to the shock room
Nothing, the marker does not work then

questions.q: When is the patient connected to the wall monitor in the shock room?
answers: By itself, when the trolley is in the shock bay
Only when the EMS monitor was left on
Only with the chief's approval on the PC
Only after the blood draw and the lab

questions.q: What must be recorded before a discharge?
answers: The result of a CT scan

questions.q: What does a risky discharge on the Ambulatory sheet mean?
answers: Sent home with unstable values (e.g. low BP)
The patient did not pay the full care fee
Brought by ambulance but left on their own
The patient did not give a citizen ID

questions.q: Who can be the treating doctor of a case?
answers: A resident or higher, after triage

questions.q: How big is the treating doctor's case bonus?
answers: 15% of the points of the closed, documented case
A fixed 100 points after every closed case
Exactly half of all the points of the case
No bonus, only the points of interventions

questions.q: How long does a lab result take?
What does the full lab contain?
answers: Every panel at once, with the blood group and tox screen
Only the blood count and the group for a transfusion
Only the cardiac markers, troponin and CK
Only the blood gas, lactate and pH for shock

questions.q: Where does the CT image show?
answers: In the result viewer and on the CT wall monitor
Only on the EMS tablet, at the task
Only on the patient's printed summary
Only on the X-ray viewer in the evening

questions.q: How many patients can be in the CT at the same time?
answers: One, the others on a queue

questions.q: Who goes first on the CT queue?
What is mandatory at an EMS handover?
answers: Give a short description of the patient
Order a full lab for the patient
Request a transfer to another hospital

questions.q: What does the allergy badge on the patient panel warn of?
What do you do when the patient takes an anticoagulant and fell?
answers: A head CT and a clotting lab are indicated
Send home when there is no visible wound
Only a dressing and a painkiller

questions.q: How often is a round on the ICU?
What is the normal sodium range?
